Package hadur2.core.model

package hadur2.core.model
The values the core is made of: what crosses the hexagonal boundary each tick, the robot states and their logs, and the waves the duel's gun and movement learn from.

The port values. BotInput is everything the core sees in a tick, with the engine's events as BotEvents, and BotOrders is everything it answers. They are immutable and compare field by field, so a battle is a list of inputs and orders that the replay can check tick for tick (CORE-2), and the core never needs robocode.* (CORE-1).

States and waves. A RobotState is a robot at one tick, and a RobotStateLog keeps a bounded history of them (RES-2), interpolating unobserved ticks. A Wave is the circle a bullet fired at one tick lies on; it converts between firing angles and guess factors, measures the precise intersection with a robot, and carries the bullet shadows our own bullets cast on an enemy wave (MOVE-1). A WaveManager holds the waves in flight on one side and reports each one as it breaks, dropping its state log (RES-2).

KNN samples. Timestamped samples, the gun's TimestampedFiringAngles and the surf's TimestampedGuessFactors, are what the KNN views store; seeded ones share a SeedWeight that keeps them lighter than live ones (ADAPT-3) and can fade them to nothing (RES-4).

Units and conventions. Robocode's throughout: pixels with the origin at the field's bottom-left and y growing upward; angles in radians, absolute ones measured from north and growing clockwise; velocities in pixels per tick; times in ticks within the round.

Dependencies. The model sits at the bottom of the core, beside hadur2.core.physics, which it uses for angles, the field and movement prediction. ArchUnit (ArchitectureTest) forbids it to depend on the gun, movement or replay packages, on opponent memory, on the adapt and policy packages, on the melee brain or on the posture gate, so any of them can use the model without a cycle. Like the rest of the core it uses only the JDK's java.lang, java.util and java.awt.geom (CORE-1), with no randomness, threads, reflection, I/O or clock (RES-6), and no mutable static fields (CORE-2).

    MaxEscapeTarget
    The result of a precise maximum-escape-angle prediction: how far, as an angle seen from a wave's source, the target can get from its bearing at fire time before the wave reaches it, and where it would be then.
    RobotState
    A robot's position and motion at one tick: ours or the enemy's, observed, interpolated or predicted.
    RobotState.Builder
    Builds a RobotState; each setter returns the builder.
    RobotStateLog
    A robot's RobotStates keyed by tick, with linear interpolation across the ticks that were not observed.
    RobotStateLog.AllStateListener
    Receives each state from RobotStateLog.forAllStates(hadur2.core.model.RobotStateLog.AllStateListener).
    SeedWeight
    The weight a group of seeded samples carries in the KNN views (ADAPT-3).
    Timestamped
    A sample stored in a KNN view, stamped with when it was observed.
    TimestampedFiringAngle
    One of the gun's KNN samples: where the enemy went relative to one of our waves, logged by GunController when the wave breaks on it (or replayed from a gun seed).
    TimestampedGuessFactor
    One of the surf's KNN samples: the guess factor at which an enemy wave met us, or at which one of its bullets hit us, logged by MoveController (or replayed from a surf seed).
    Wave
    A wave: the circle a bullet fired at Wave.fireTime from Wave.sourceLocation would lie on, growing by Wave.bulletSpeed() pixels every tick.
    Wave.Intersection
    A range of absolute firing angles from a wave's source: a centre and a half-width.
    Wave.WavePosition
    Where a wave is relative to a robot, in the order a wave passes through them; see Wave.checkWavePosition(RobotState, boolean, WavePosition).
    WaveManager
    The waves in flight on one side of the duel, and the bookkeeping that decides when each one has passed its target.
    WaveManager.AllWaveListener

    WaveManager.WaveBreakListener
